description: Benchmark workload: 150 prompts an internal company assistant might get, none taken from intelligence/eval/routing-set.json (the set the classifier was tuned on). Categories are the team's own labels, used only to break results down; the gateway never sees them. easy: lookups, conversions, rewrites, extraction, chat. hard: code, maths, analysis, long-form, high-stakes advice, long context. time_sensitive: needs current information.
system_prompt: You are a helpful assistant in a company's internal workspace. Answer clearly and concisely.

Here are notes from our launch review: The mobile app release is planned for 2 December. QA found that push notifications fail on Android 14 for about 8% of devices; Karthik thinks it is a permissions change but hasn't confirmed. The payments team (Divya) is still waiting on the bank's sandbox credentials, which were promised three weeks ago. Marketing has booked a press briefing for 3 December, the day after launch. Support has not been trained on the new refund flow, and the help-centre articles are still drafts. Legal approved the new terms of service, but the privacy policy update is waiting for review by the data protection officer, who is on leave until 28 November. Identify the three biggest risks to the launch date, explain why, and suggest an owner and a next step for each.

Customer email: "I ordered a standing desk (order 55102) on 2 November. It arrived on the 9th with a cracked leg, so I raised a return. Your courier came on the 12th but refused to take it because the box wasn't the original one, which nobody told me I needed. Meanwhile I was charged a restocking fee of 1,200 rupees even though the desk was damaged on arrival. I also asked twice for an invoice with my company's GST number and got no reply." Draft a reply that addresses every complaint, says what we will do about each, and keeps a warm, professional tone.
